name: Cost Price, Selling Price, Profit and Loss Basics
description: Understand C.P., S.P., profit and loss, and calculate gain or loss percentages from the correct base.
script_scope: Build the meaning of cost price and selling price before formulas. Teach profit = S.P. − C.P. and loss = C.P. − S.P., with gain/loss percentage always reckoned on cost price. Move between C.P., S.P., absolute gain/loss and percentage, including decimal percentages and simple ratio views such as C.P.:S.P. Prepare learners for direct exam questions asking profit percent, loss percent, or whether a transaction is a gain or loss. Use mental 100-based models before general formulas and check by comparing S.P. back with C.P.

name: Reverse Cost Price, Selling Price and Changed Price
description: Work backward from a known profit or loss percentage, and solve questions where a different selling price changes loss into profit.
script_scope: Teach reverse percentage reasoning: if a sale at 20% loss gives an S.P., that S.P. is 80% of C.P.; if a sale at 25% gain gives an S.P., it is 125% of C.P. Use this to recover C.P., then compare alternate selling prices. Cover questions where a fixed rupee change turns a loss into a gain, where one selling price gives a known profit and another gives a different profit/loss, and where C.P. itself changes before resale. Emphasize the percentage-point gap method when two outcomes share the same C.P., and verify by reconstructing both selling prices.

name: Total Cost, Overheads, Wastage and Unsold Stock
description: Include repairs, transport, installation, damaged goods, fixed overheads and unsold stock before judging the real profit or loss.
script_scope: Teach that real cost includes all amounts spent to make goods sale-ready: purchase, repairs, transport, octroi, installation and fixed overheads when the question includes them. Cover broken/rejected/unsold units, useful output after wastage, per-unit target selling price, and simple break-even with fixed cost plus variable cost. Distinguish sunk cost of all units from revenue earned only on saleable units. Include quality-rejection and production examples shaped like the objective exercise. Learners should total the outlay first, then decide the required total revenue, then divide by units actually sold.

name: Quantity Rates and Item Equivalences
description: Handle ‘x for ₹y’, dozens, C.P. of one quantity equals S.P. of another, and profit equal to the price of some units.
script_scope: Teach quantity-price forms without converting every item separately. Use a common batch or L.C.M. for statements such as bought 6 for ₹10 and sold 4 for ₹6. Cover C.P. of m articles = S.P. of n articles, gain/loss equal to S.P. or C.P. of some units, how many items per rupee must be bought or sold for a target gain, and free-item offers as an effective discount. Keep the unit meaning visible so learners do not invert buying and selling rates. End with a capstone combining a quantity equivalence with a target percentage.

name: Combined Lots and Partial Sales
description: Find overall profit or loss when different parts of the same stock are sold at different rates or percentages.
script_scope: Teach that overall profit is based on total cost, not the average of percentage labels unless the cost bases are equal. Cover two goods with different cost prices and gain/loss rates, a fraction of a consignment sold at one rate and the rest at another, finding an unknown cost split from overall profit, and finding what rate the remaining stock must fetch to reach a target overall profit. Include same-total-cost and unequal-cost cases, plus damaged or leftover stock where appropriate. Use contribution tables mentally: cost part → selling multiplier → sale amount → total.

name: Mixtures and Weighted Cost in Profit Problems
description: Combine goods bought at different rates, find the true mean cost, and set a selling rate for a target profit.
script_scope: Teach weighted cost per unit for mixtures: total cost divided by total quantity. Cover two and three purchase rates, equal-quantity traps, ratio-weighted mixtures, selling a blend at a target profit, recovering an unknown component cost, and using alligation only after converting a desired selling price back to the required mean cost. Include milk/water or tea/rice style commercial mixtures when the key skill is profit on the blend. Keep this lesson focused on cost weighting rather than general mixture theory.

name: Successive Traders and Price Chains
description: Track an article through manufacturer, wholesaler, retailer and later buyers as each stage adds a profit or loss multiplier.
script_scope: Teach a price chain as successive multipliers: each trader’s selling price becomes the next trader’s cost price. Cover two- and three-hand transactions, recovering the first cost from the final price, finding a missing trader profit when overall rise is known, chains containing a loss at one stage, and reverse-working through the chain. Distinguish percentage profit on each trader’s own cost from percentage change relative to the original cost. Use compact multiplier chains such as ×1.20 ×1.25 ×1.10.

name: Two Articles, Equal Gain and Loss, and Overall Result
description: Understand why equal gain and loss percentages on two equal selling prices do not cancel, and solve paired-item transactions.
script_scope: Teach paired transactions with a total-cost view. Cover two articles sold at the same S.P., one at x% gain and one at x% loss, derive the inevitable loss and connect it to the book’s x²/100 rule. Also cover unequal gain/loss percentages, equal absolute profit and loss at two selling prices, recovering C.P. as the midpoint when gain and loss amounts are equal, and splitting a total cost between two items from the overall result. Learners should not average percentages blindly; they must reconstruct the cost bases.

name: Marked Price, Discount and Profit
description: Connect cost price, marked price, discount and final selling price in one clear price ladder.
script_scope: Teach the ladder C.P. → marked price → discount → S.P. Start from one markup and one discount, then reverse to find M.P., C.P., discount or required markup for a target profit. Cover marked price given as a percentage above cost, discount as a percentage of marked price, no-discount profit comparisons, and rupee discount amounts. Show why equal markup and discount percentages do not cancel because they use different bases. Include exam-style questions with list/labelled price terminology.

name: Successive Discounts, Commission, Tax and Net Price
description: Handle several price layers such as two discounts, commission, sales tax/VAT and extra charges without mixing their bases.
script_scope: Teach successive discounts as multipliers rather than addition, find the single equivalent discount, recover one missing discount, and combine markup with trade/cash discount. Add commission as a deduction from retail price when the source uses it, and sales tax/VAT as a layer on the selling price where applicable. Cover final bill versus pre-tax S.P., and questions asking what profit would have been without a discount. Keep each percentage attached to its own base and use a price ladder to prevent base confusion.

name: False Weights, Measures and Adulteration
description: See how short weights, false scales and free adulterants change the trader’s real cost per delivered unit.
script_scope: Teach dishonest-dealer questions from first principles before shortcuts. If a trader charges for 1 kg but delivers 960 g, compare money received for 1 kg with the cost of only 960 g. Cover false metre scales, nominal profit or loss combined with short weight, cheating while both buying and selling, and milk/water adulteration where water has zero cost. Show the book’s shortcut formulas only after the 100-unit model makes them intuitive. Check all gains against actual cost delivered.

name: Profit Bases, Ratios and Algebraic Price Relations
description: Translate unusual statements such as profit as a fraction of S.P., C.P.:S.P. ratios, doubled selling price and symbolic price relations.
script_scope: Cover advanced wording where the usual percentage base is disguised. Teach profit or loss stated as a fraction/percentage of S.P., convert between profit-on-S.P. and profit-on-C.P., use C.P.:S.P. ratios, and solve relations such as doubling S.P. triples profit or a numerical profit percent equals the C.P. Include symbolic forms with p, q and r, equal percentage profit/loss at two prices, and short equations created from changed selling prices. The core habit is to label C.P., S.P. and profit amount before forming an equation.

name: Data Sufficiency for Profit and Loss
description: Decide whether one statement, the other, both, or neither give enough information to determine a profit-and-loss answer.
script_scope: Teach data sufficiency as a uniqueness test, not a full-calculation contest. Use C.P./S.P./profit questions, ratios, marked price and discount, mixture selling price, quantity equivalences, and three-statement variants shaped like the chapter’s separate data-sufficiency exercise. Learners should test statement I alone, reset, test statement II alone, then combine only if needed. Include cases where a statement is merely a consequence of another, where either statement alone works, where both are required, and where even all supplied data are insufficient.
